chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a Jew who had been immoral with a Muslim woman. He said: 'He should be killed'.

key_terms.فَجَرَ: To commit illicit sexual intercourse or be immoral; here referring to zinā (adultery/fornication)
key_terms.يَهُودِيٍّ: A Jew, specifically referring to a male from the People of the Book in this context
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: He is killed / He should be executed

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd penalty for a Jew who commits adultery with a Muslim woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the specific penalty for a Jewish man from the Ahl al-Zimma who commits illicit sexual intercourse with a Muslim woman is established as execution. This hadith highlights the principle of applying the hadd penalty strictly based on the act and the status of the parties, reflecting the juristic consensus in Shia fiqh regarding the sexual integrity of Muslim women under the protection of the Islamic state. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how non-Muslim subjects were subject to Islamic penal codes in matters of public morality.
